subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — HIPAA, BAA, SOC2 evidence
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Ross <alan.ross@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode qualification follow-up — HIPAA / SOC2 

Hi Alan —

Thanks for taking the time today — great to learn more about Elara's workflow and compliance needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Recap:
- Primary constraint: storing/processing PHI for clinical notes and attachments. Elara requires a signed BAA and SOC 2 Type II evidence.
- Key security asks: customer-managed KMS (HSM/KMS integration), audit logs (immutable, exportable), data retention/erase controls, network isolation, and ability to restrict egress.
- Volume: estimated 50M tokens/month initially; peak concurrency ~25 qps.

Redwood deployment guidance (high level):
- Hosted API + BAA: fastest to run, available for vetted customers with limited PHI use cases; good for early pilots but may have limitations on dedicated encryption controls and network isolation.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): recommended for production PHI workloads that need stronger isolation, optional KMS integrations, and more predictable performance and SLAs. Supports audit logging and configurable retention.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended if Elara requires full private control plane, on-prem key management, or air-gapped deployments for regulated environments.

Attachments I attached: a redacted version of our most recent SOC2 Type II, a BAA template, and a short deployment-mode comparison workbook.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm the minimal encryption/KMS requirements (customer-managed keys required? HSM vs cloud KMS).
2) Can your compliance team (cc'd compliance@elarahealth.com) share any SOC2 or audit scoping questions we should address?
3) I'll loop in Rishi and Dylan for a technical deep-dive. Can you share 2x 1-hour slots next week for an engineering call?
4) If the requirements align, we'll provide a preliminary sizing and price estimate for Dedicated vs Private.

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your priority list.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: SOC2_TypeII_2025_redacted.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)
Attachment: Redwood_BAA_template_v1.docx (DOCX, 48KB)
Attachment: deployment_mode_comparison.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)

From: Alan Ross <alan.ross@elarahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elara Health Compliance <compliance@elarahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — HIPAA / SOC2

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the materials. A few clarifications from our side to help prioritize: 

1) BAA: yes, we need a signed BAA before any PHI is sent. Please confirm you can sign Elara's standard BAA or we can start from your template.
2) SOC2 evidence: we need the most recent Type II report. The redacted copy you sent looks fine; our auditors will likely want confirmation of the covered services and controls mapping (encryption, access control, incident response).
3) KMS: Customer-managed keys are required for production PHI. We prefer an HSM-backed KMS (Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS with CloudHSM). Does Dedicated support BYOK/HSM integrations?
4) Audit logs & retention: we need immutable audit logs for 7 years and the ability to export logs to our SIEM.
5) Network: we will want VPC peering or PrivateLink options for low-trust network boundary.

Also — cost question: can you provide a ballpark monthly cost range for Dedicated vs Private for the volumes we discussed (50M tokens/month, 25 qps peak)? We understand this is rough.

We can do a technical call next Tuesday 6/30 or Wednesday 7/1 between 10-2 PT. Please include your engineering/security folks.

Thanks,
Alan Ross
Head of Platform Engineering | Elara Health
alan.ross@elarahealth.com | (617) 555-9876

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Ross <alan.ross@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Elara Health Compliance <compliance@elarahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — HIPAA / SOC2

Thanks for the specifics — helpful. Quick answers inline, plus next steps and links: 

1) BAA: We can start from our Redwood_BAA_template_v1.docx (attached) and are open to signing Elara's standard BAA after legal review. I'll flag this to our Legal.
2) SOC2: That redacted report covers the Redwood Inference control scope for our hosted and dedicated offerings. I'll include a short controls mapping doc in follow-up if helpful (we have a mapping that points to encryption, access control, logging, and incident response controls).
3) KMS/HSM: Yes — Dedicated supports BYOK integrations. We integrate with AWS KMS (CloudHSM) and Azure Key Vault for HSM-backed keys. Private (VPC/on-prem) provides the most flexibility if you need full on-prem HSM.
4) Audit logs & retention: We can export immutable audit logs to an S3 bucket or push to SIEM via our export pipeline. Retention policies can be configured; 7-year retention is supported for exported logs (we'll need to confirm long-term storage options/costs).
5) Network: We support PrivateLink and VPC peering for Dedicated; Private gives full control.

Cost ballpark (very rough):
- Dedicated (reserved): ~$30k-~$75k/month depending on instance class, reserved commitment, and throughput needs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): higher initial setup + infra costs; monthly OPEX varies widely (estimate starting ~$60k/month for comparable throughput with more op-ex support).

Next steps proposed:
- Sign BAA (Legal loop) — I can send our tracked BAA and request Elara's for review.
- Technical deep-dive: proposed Tue 30 Jun 2026 @ 10:30 PT (60 min) — Rishi will cover infra/KMS/audit logs, Dylan will cover deployment/ops and SLOs.
- I'll prepare a short controls-mapping doc and a preliminary Dedicated sizing estimate prior to the call.

Please confirm the slot and whether compliance wants any specific agenda items.

Best,
Marissa

Alan, Marissa —

Thanks — I'll join the call today at 10:30 PT. Agenda I propose (30-45m technical + 15m open Q&A):
1) Quick intro & scope (5m)
2) Data flows & PHI touchpoints (10m) — I need a short inventory of data types and where PHI will be processed/stored.
3) KMS details & BYOK flow (10m) — how keys are provisioned, rotation, and access model (we support AWS KMS + CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault with HSM; we can also accommodate external HSM with Private).
4) Audit logs & export (10m) — formats, immutability, and export pipeline to S3/SIEM.
5) Pilot plan & POC options (10m) — recommend a short Dedicated pilot with log export to your S3 and a control checklist.

Actions before call (please):
- Alan/team: share 1-page inventory of PHI categories and any vendor questionnaire items you care most about.
- Compliance: if you have a SOC2 scoping checklist or specific control mappings, please share ahead so we can address.

Forwarding Marissa's note for context.

Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
